provenance.pipeline: satsuki v1 (v1.0.1 editorial re-edit: usage-note reshaping corpus-wide, lane discrimination for same-surface families, against prompts/style.md)

patterns.usage_note: Takes an action or state stated as a clause for its standard, then reports a result that standard would not predict, so the mismatch is the news: 毎日練習しているにしては上達が遅い. The sibling lane takes the same string when the standard is a category the subject belongs to and the comment rates it inside that category (チワワにしちゃよく食べる). It attaches straight to a plain clause, where わりに needs の after a noun (値段の割に).

examples.ruby: 一日[いちにち]で仕上[しあ]げたにしては、上出来[じょうでき]だと思[おも]う。
examples.english: For something finished in a single day, I'd say it came out well.

examples.ruby: あれだけ道[みち]に迷[まよ]ったにしては、ずいぶん早[はや]く着[つ]いたね。
examples.english: For how lost we got, we made it here pretty early.

examples.ruby: 毎日[まいにち]練習[れんしゅう]しているにしては、上達[じょうたつ]が遅[おそ]い気[き]がする。
examples.english: For someone who practices every day, I feel like they're improving slowly.

patterns.usage_note: Weighs a result against the degree the first clause sets up, reporting more or less than that degree would predict (狭い割に品揃えが豊富だ, 五キロ走った割に疲れていない). It takes gradable material, i-adjectives included, where にしては wants a nameable standard, and unlike くせに it carries no reproach. A noun of scale attaches through の (値段の割に). The adverb 割に / 割と ('fairly, comparatively') is a separate word.

examples.ruby: この店[みせ]は狭[せま]い割[わり]に品揃[しなぞろ]えが豊富[ほうふ]だ。
examples.english: For such a cramped shop, it carries a surprising range.

examples.ruby: 五[ご]キロも走[はし]った割[わり]に、まったく疲[つか]れていない。
examples.english: Considering I ran five kilometers, I'm not tired in the slightest.

examples.ruby: 値段[ねだん]の割[わり]に、この鞄[かばん]は縫[ぬ]い目[め]が粗[あら]い。
examples.english: For what it costs, the stitching on this bag is sloppy.

patterns.usage_note: Marks a reproachful contradiction: the speaker criticizes or mocks someone whose behavior clashes with what they are (子供のくせに大人びた口をきく). Both clauses normally share one subject and that subject is normally a person, which is why くせに cannot replace every のに. It attaches to a noun through の and to a na-adjective through な; くせして is blunter and out of place about anyone senior.

examples.ruby: 本当[ほんとう]は知[し]っているくせに、何[なに]も教[おし]えてくれない。
examples.english: He knows perfectly well, and yet he won't tell me a thing.

examples.ruby: あいつは毎回[まいかい]遅[おく]れてくるくせして、平気[へいき]な顔[かお]をしている。
examples.english: He turns up late every single time and still has the nerve to look unbothered.

examples.ruby: 子供[こども]のくせに、ずいぶん大人[おとな]びた口[くち]をきく。
examples.english: Quite the grown-up way of talking, for a kid.
